key_findings: Substack public RSS feed pattern is /feed (not /feed.xml). e.g. https://a16zcrypto.substack.com/feed — confirmed working. Every Substack newsletter has this by default for public posts
Paid-only content is NOT in the public RSS feed — only free/preview posts. To get paid content, need subscriber-specific RSS or email forwarding
a16z crypto RSS confirmed: https://a16zcrypto.substack.com/feed — can scrape with existing RSS adapter (same as Cointelegraph)
Milk Road, Bankless, Coinstack RSS feeds NOT confirmed from search — need to verify by fetching their Substack pages and checking /feed endpoint
Email-based newsletter ingestion without IMAP: Gmail filter + forwarding to email-to-webhook service (EmailConnect, Zapier, or custom SMTP). Gmail auto-forwards to alias that POSTs JSON to webhook

RSS feed detection for sites without explicit link: (1) check HTML <head> for autodiscovery <link> tags, (2) try common paths (/feed, /rss, /rss.xml, /atom.xml), (3) check sitemap.xml, (4) crawl visible links for feed/rss/atom patterns
Dedup across email AND RSS: use content hash (SHA256 of title + body snippet) — same newsletter arriving via both paths gets deduped by hash, keep whichever arrives first
uncertainties: Milk Road and Bankless Substack RSS endpoints not confirmed — need to fetch each /feed and validate
Whether Coinstack is actually on Substack or a separate platform — domain unknown
Whether Gmail forwarding + webhook service adds latency vs direct RSS polling (email is push-based, RSS is pull-based)
Whether email-to-webhook services have rate limits or per-message costs
